title: Batching Sherlock Scratchpad
content:
Goal: incremental breadcrumbs for the throughput regression during the Jan 28-31 rollout (dedicated pools, continuous-batcher changes). Personal notebook style — rough, keep or toss.

Summary so far
- Symptom: 20–40% per-shard throughput regression (p50/p95 latency ok, token cost up) starting 2025-01-29 03:00 UTC after small runtime change that touched continuous-batcher heuristics + KV prefetch path.
- Scope: affected shards running m-cpu-alt and g4nv2 profiles in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Not all shards; seems traffic-pattern dependent (many short requests).
- Immediate impact: unit-cost up ~18% for some customers; one internal regression alert fired (RED-8152).
- Hypothesis primaries: batching window mis-tuned (window_ms too small for pattern), KV prefetch causing cache churn, or scheduler change introduced priority inversion under microbursts.

What I tried (commands, config toggles) — chronological notes
1) Quick repro (local-ish):
- hammer script: python tools/loadgen/poisson_client.py --host api.internal.redwood --concurrency 32 --pattern short-queries --duration 90s --model x-small
- Observed: CPU utilization fine; batch sizes peaked at 1–2 (bad). When I force longer client think-time, batch sizes come back up.

2) Telemetry queries (PromQL snippets used)
- rate(batcher_observed_batch_size[5m]) -> showed mean downshift from ~8 to ~2 around 2025-01-29T02:58:00Z.
- sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total[5m])) by (shard) -> spike correlated with throughput drop on same shards.
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, shard)) -> p95 stayed stable for most but p50 moved slightly.

3) Configuration toggles (performed on a small canary pool)
- continuous_batch.window_ms: rollback from 25 -> 100 on canary for 1 hour. Result: batch sizes increased from mean 2 -> 7, throughput returned close to baseline.
- continuous_batch.max_window_ms: temporarily raised 250->500 (no immediate impact beyond window_ms change).
- kv.prefetch.enabled: false on canary. Result: KV miss rate dropped but batching remained small unless window_ms increased. Suggests prefetch amplifies problem but not root cause.

4) Instrumentation dumps (selected snippets)
- batch_scheduler trace: "saw candidate at t=1614355510.234; holding buffer for 5ms then flushed because window_count==1 and max_hold_ms reached"
- kernel log: "prefetch: enqueued 3 keys, inflight=6, eviction_candidate=shard-12"
- error snippets: "WARN batcher: small-batch-flush threshold met repeatedly for shard shard-17 (concurrency=64)"

5) Replayed traffic against previous runtime (2025-01-25 commit) in staging
- Using same traffic mix, old runtime produced mean batch size 8 and stable throughput. New runtime produced batch size 2. Confirms behavioral regression.

Quick actionable hypothesis (working)
- The change to continuous-batcher heuristics swapped from a latency-first policy to an adaptive policy that aggressively flushes small batches when per-request estimated latency risk > threshold. Under high short-query ratio this policy degrades batching because it overestimates risk when KV prefetch spikes latency variance.
- Secondary amplifier: a change in KV prefetch concurrency (default 6 -> 12) increased transient KV misses/evictions which raised per-request latency variance, which in turn triggered the adaptive flusher more often.

Notes on causation vs correlation
- Correlation: timing aligns — rollout included both CBATCH heuristic tweaks and KV prefetch concurrency bump.
- Causation evidence: rollback of window_ms alone on canary restored most throughput even with prefetch=on. So window tuning is main lever. But prefetch amplifies — disabling it improves tail, increases confidence that both contributed.

Things to try next (ordered)
1) Run controlled matrix on canary pool: (window_ms = [25,50,100,200]) x (prefetch_concurrency = [3,6,12]) x (short_query_ratio = [0.3,0.6,0.9]) — aim to capture interaction surface.
2) Add a short-window moving variance estimator to batcher heuristic that uses smoothed kv_fetch_latency_ms rather than raw instantaneous latency to decide flush. Rationale: reduces reactive flushes caused by KV miss spikes.
3) Telemetry additions: emit batcher_decision_reason label (explicit reasons: time_expired | count_limit | latency_risk | manual_flush) and sample 1% of batcher traces with full KV timings.
4) Rollback plan: if canary papers out, roll back cbatch heuristic change entirely and then re-roll a safer variant with longer windows + telemetry.

Debugging artifacts and quick links
- Repro script: tools/loadgen/poisson_client.py (branch: aisha/batch-sherlock).
- Telemetry dashboards: /dashboards/serving/batcher/short-query-regression (saved view for 2025-01-25..2025-02-07).
- GRAB logs: s3://internal-logs/rolling/serving/2025-01-29/shard-*.log (grep for "small-batch-flush").

Hypotheses I want to test but low priority
- Scheduler priority inversion: under specific burst arrival patterns, queue priority weights cause high-priority small requests to starve batch-accumulation for normal priority. To test: enable debug priority counters and simulate mixed-priority traffic.
- Quantization kernel path disparity: if some shards fall back to slower kernels under small batches, that would increase latency variance causing more flushes. I did a quick check; no kernel switch coincident with regression on canary.

Random notes / brain-dump (keep for context)
- Why did we change window_ms? original change was to try to avoid p95 regressions in very long requests (making the flusher more conservative for large sequences). Tweak accidentally impacted short-request mix.
- Someone (PR author) left comment: "adaptive_threshold now uses sample stddev across 20 samples" — but we ship with sample size=3 by default. Might be unstable.
- Oncall pinged midnight of 29th: noted temporary mitigation by increasing concurrency of clients (hacky) which improved batching slightly. Not a fix.

Checklist before writing a postmortem
- Reproduce matrix results + attach CSV of batch size distributions per config.
- Confirm root cause by rolling back cbatch heuristic in prod canary and observing metrics for 24h.
- Draft blameless timeline with deploy IDs and PR authors.
- Add recommendations: telemetry labels, safe default window_ms (100ms?), conservative prefetch_concurrency default (3), and rollout gating via traffic-shape tests.

Open questions (to discuss in sync)
- What rollout gating did we have for heuristics? Did Jenkins job include short-query-heavy traffic tests?
- Should prefetch_concurrency be a per-model tunable? Might differ widely by model size and KV locality.

Next immediate steps (today)
- Kick off matrix runs on canary (Benji volunteered to help). Command template: ./scripts/run_matrix.sh --pool canary-3 --config matrix.csv --out s3://tmp/aisha/batch-matrix-20250207.csv
- Add diagnostic counter batcher_decision_reason (quick patch) and ship to canary; run for 2h and collect.

If this grows into an incident doc, move findings into shared_drives/company/misc/ and notify product/sales for impacted customers list (I left a note in RED-8152).

Notes to self: keep this in users so I can iteratively change. If we converge on fix, produce a cleaned PRD and postmortem in shared drive.

-- Aisha
